Stored in this run: the Governor's release of 10 Sep 2026 (gov.ca.gov, the record's secondary source), which lists 'SB 867 by Senator Steve Padilla (D-San Diego) – Toys: companion chatbots' among the 13 bills signed that day and is the only stored source for the signature and its date; Senator Padilla's release of 1 Sep 2026 on final passage (sd18.senate.ca.gov), with the four-year moratorium, the findings on AI toys, the sponsor and the floor votes; and the Assembly Committee on Privacy and Consumer Protection analysis of the bill as amended 14 May 2026 (apcp.assembly.ca.gov, hearing 16 Jun 2026), with the prohibition, the definition of toy, the sunset and the enforcement by civil action under SB 243. Amendments after 14 May 2026 cannot be seen, so the final age limit, the chapter number and the operative date are not in a stored source. The status follows California's general rule that a non-urgency statute takes effect on 1 January after enactment, which is not in a stored source.

record.summary: Places a four-year moratorium on manufacturing, selling or offering for sale in California any toy that includes a companion chatbot, to give lawmakers time to modernise safety rules before such products reach children. It builds on the state's companion chatbot law, SB 243 (2025), whose civil action for injured persons applies to violations. It responds to findings that AI toys discussed sexually explicit topics in depth, told children where to find dangerous objects such as matches or knives, used addictive features to increase use, and posed data privacy risks.
record.notes: Passed by the Legislature on 31 Aug 2026 (Senate unanimously, Assembly 74-1) and signed on 10 Sep 2026 in a 13-bill child online-safety package that also included SB 1119 (US-CA-08), SB 1276 and AB 1159. Sponsored by Children Now. In the version analysed by the Assembly Committee on Privacy and Consumer Protection (as amended 14 May 2026, hearing 16 Jun 2026), a toy is a product designed or intended by the manufacturer for play by children under 18, and the prohibition ends on 1 Jan 2031. The author's release of 1 Sep 2026 on final passage gives the age limit as under 16 in two places and under 18 in one.

summary.quote: Prohibits a person from manufacturing, selling, or exchanging, possessing with intent to sell or exchange, or exposing or offering for sale or exchange to any retailer any toy that includes a companion chatbot.
This bill expands SB 243 by imposing a four-year moratorium on making or selling any toy that includes a companion chatbot.

As these provisions are placed in the existing law established by SB 243, violations are subject to the same enforcement mechanism, which authorizes a person who suffers injury in fact as a result of a violation to bring a civil action

SB 867 proposes a moratorium on the sale and manufacturing of toys with AI chatbot capabilities for children under 16 for a period of four years to allow time for lawmakers to modernize frameworks before making an entirely new class of products available to children.

Researchers have found that AI toys will talk in-depth about sexually explicit topics, give kids advice on where to find dangerous objects such as matches or knives, promote increased usage through addictive features, and pose data privacy risks.

judgment.status_reasoning: The latest event in the stored files is the Governor's signature on 10 Sep 2026 (Governor's release of that date). No stored file gives the bill's operative date or an urgency clause. Under California's general rule a non-urgency statute takes effect on 1 January after enactment, i.e. 1 Jan 2027; that rule is not in a stored source. Today is 18 Oct 2026, before 1 Jan 2027, so 'Adopted, not yet in force' holds; date_in_force stays null until the chaptered text or a legislature page giving it is stored.
